goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:11 — `@topic_view = TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` — `TopicView` class not found anywhere in repo; raises NameError on every repeat view of an already-embedded topic (confidence=85, P0).

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbedController#best` which instantiates `TopicView`, but the claim that `TopicView` is “not found anywhere in repo” is not verifiable from this diff. In fact, the diff’s own new spec (`spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`) expects `TopicView.expects(:new)` to be called, implying `TopicView` is an existing class in the codebase (common in Discourse) rather than a newly missing constant. Nothing in the diff indicates `TopicView` was removed or renamed, so a NameError is not a defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:47 — `doc = Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` — file never requires 'open-uri'; if PollFeed hasn't been autoloaded first, `open(url)` resolves to plain Kernel#open (file path semantics) not URI fetch, breaking the async retrieve path (confidence=75, P1).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.import_remote` which calls `open(url).read` but `app/models/topic_embed.rb` does not `require 'open-uri'`. Other new code paths call `import_remote` without requiring open-uri first (e.g., `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` and `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`), so `open("http://...")` can resolve to plain `Kernel#open` and fail with local-file semantics (e.g., Errno::ENOENT) unless some unrelated boot code has already loaded open-uri. The only explicit `require 'open-uri'` in the diff is in `Jobs::PollFeed`, which doesn’t cover these other call sites. This is a concrete correctness bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:2 — `require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'` — that file does not exist in the repo; spec fails to load (confidence=70, P2).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new spec file `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` with `require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'`, and the diff itself does not add `jobs/regular/process_post`. However, whether that required file exists (or existed prior to this change) cannot be verified from the provided diff alone. The finding asserts a repo-wide absence that isn't demonstrated here, so it relies on information outside the diff rather than a verifiable defect introduced by it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` — no rescue for network/timeout/malformed-XML failures; `retry: false` silently drops the hourly poll; poll_feed_spec never calls real poll_feed logic (confidence=85, P1).

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no exception handling. Both `open` (network/DNS/timeout/HTTP errors) and `SimpleRSS.parse` (malformed/empty XML) can raise, which would cause the scheduled job execution to fail. The job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so Sidekiq will not retry on failure (it will just fail that run and wait until the next scheduled occurrence). Also, the added spec `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only asserts `execute` delegates (or not) to `poll_feed` based on settings; it never exercises the actual network/parse/import path, so these failures are untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:3-7,25 — `validates_presence_of` only, no `validates_uniqueness_of :embed_url` mirroring the DB unique index; concurrent imports of same URL can raise unhandled RecordNotUnique/RecordInvalid leaving orphan Topic/Post (confidence=70, P1).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a unique DB index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` but the model only validates presence. However, the claimed defect (“missing validates_uniqueness_of mirrors DB index; concurrent imports can leave orphan Topic/Post”) is not verifiable from the diff: `TopicEmbed.import` wraps the PostCreator + TopicEmbed.create! in a `Topic.transaction`, so if the unique index is hit and `create!` raises, the transaction should roll back the post/topic created in that block rather than leaving orphans. Also, adding `validates_uniqueness_of` would not reliably prevent concurrent duplicates anyway (it’s subject to the same race), so the finding’s proposed root cause/impact is overstated and not clearly a real bug introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:32-33 — `url = i.link; url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//` — if both link and id are invalid, invalid url silently passed to TopicEmbed.import which silently no-ops, no logging, untested (confidence=75, P2).

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the code falls back from `i.link` to `i.id` when `link` is blank or not an absolute http(s) URL. If the resulting `url` is still not an absolute http(s) URL, `TopicEmbed.import` immediately returns (`return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`), so the feed item is simply skipped with no logging. That behavior is verifiably present, and there is no test covering this URL-selection/skip path in `poll_feed`. However, skipping malformed/unsupported URLs without logging is not clearly a defect introduced by the diff; it may be an intentional “ignore invalid items” behavior rather than a bug/security/correctness error. The finding is therefore more of an observability/enhancement suggestion than a clear problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/site_settings.yml:353 — `feed_polling_url: ''` declared with no url-format validator despite feeding directly into `open(...)` (confidence=70, P2).
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `feed_polling_url` lacks URL-format validation even though it is used in `open(...)`, which aligns with the golden issue of unvalidated user-controlled URL leading to arbitrary fetch/SSRF behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:36-46 — check-then-act `perform_retrieve` has no locking beyond a 60s redis throttle scoped differently than the poll_feed race; untested for concurrency (confidence=60, P2).

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, `perform_retrieve` does a classic TOCTOU sequence: it first checks `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` and, if false, proceeds to import via `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` and/or `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. There is no lock around this check+create path. The only guard is `retrieved_recently?`, a 60s Redis `setnx` throttle keyed by `retrieved:#{@embed_url}`, which is not a true mutual exclusion (and can be bypassed with `no_throttle`, or hit by concurrent workers before the key is set/observed). Since `topic_embeds.embed_url` has a unique index and `TopicEmbed.import` uses `TopicEmbed.create!` without rescuing uniqueness violations, concurrent calls can raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` even though the code pre-checks `exists?`. This is a real concurrency/correctness risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9-10 — `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)` has no format validation at controller boundary (javascript:/data: schemes accepted); untested for malformed input (confidence=65, P2).
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:1-41 — entire new RSS/Atom feed-polling job/feature is out of scope for "embed URL handling and validation" (confidence=90, P1).

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding is about scope (“entire new RSS/Atom feed-polling job/feature is out of scope for embed URL handling and validation”), which is a process/product decision rather than a bug, security issue, or correctness defect that can be verified from the diff. The diff explicitly adds feed polling settings, a scheduled job (Jobs::PollFeed), and integration in TopicRetriever/TopicEmbed as part of the embedding feature; nothing in the diff indicates this is unintended or broken solely because it expands scope. Therefore it is not a real, verifiable problem in the code changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:114-146 — removes previously-working `--category` CLI option/logic with no relation to the stated embed task; unrelated regression (confidence=90, P1).

adjudication.rationale: The diff in lib/tasks/disqus.thor explicitly removes the `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` declaration and deletes the associated `category_id` lookup logic, and the post/topic creation code no longer passes any category information (it now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)`). This is a concrete, verifiable breaking change/regression for users who previously relied on `disqus import --category ...` to control where imported topics were created, with no alternative shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Gemfile:209-211 — `ruby-readability`/`simple-rss` gems added, the latter solely supporting the out-of-scope RSS importer (confidence=75, P2).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new functionality for embedding and feed importing. `simple-rss` is actually required by new in-scope code (`Jobs::PollFeed` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`), and that job is invoked from `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. Likewise, `ruby-readability` is used by `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb`) and is called from both `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` and the modified `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`. The claim that `simple-rss` is "solely supporting an out-of-scope RSS importer" is a scope assertion not verifiable from the diff, and dependency additions for new features are not inherently a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:83-86 — `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` modifies the shared/global post-revision engine used by all edits, broader than embed scope, and weakens rather than adds validation (confidence=70, P2).

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostRevisor#update_post` from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, meaning validations are still enforced by default and are only skipped when an internal caller explicitly passes `skip_validations: true` (as done in this same diff by `TopicEmbed.import`). The finding’s claim that this broadly “weakens validation” as a defect is not verifiable from the diff alone because there’s no evidence that untrusted/user-controlled code can set `skip_validations` on normal edits; the change appears to implement intended behavior for system imports rather than introduce a clear bug/security issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:37-38 + post_revisor — embed import path explicitly disables post validations (`skip_validations: true`) on both create and update, contradicting the task's "validation system" framing (confidence=75, P2).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `skip_validations: true` being passed on create (TopicEmbed.import -> PostCreator) and on update (PostRevisor.revise! with `skip_validations: true`), and PostRevisor is modified to honor that by saving with `validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]`. However, this is an explicit, intentional import-mode behavior in the new embedding/feed-import feature, and the diff itself provides no requirement or invariant indicating validations must run for these imports. Without evidence in the diff that bypassing validations causes incorrectness/security issues (beyond the intended import), the finding is not a verifiable defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:63-65 — new `cook_methods` enum/column alters core Post rendering pipeline app-wide, a core-engine change bundled into an embed-scoped task (confidence=60, P2).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a new `posts.cook_method` column and a `Post.cook_methods` enum, and `Post#cook` now branches on it. However, the migration sets `cook_method` default to `1` and the enum is defined as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`, meaning existing/normal posts will continue using the default (regular) cooking pipeline unless explicitly set to `:raw_html` (as done only for imported embeds). So while this is a cross-cutting/core change, the finding frames it as a problematic “embed-scoped task” bundling issue rather than identifying a concrete defect (bug/security/correctness regression) introduced by the diff. The change is opt-in and does not verifiably break app-wide rendering by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26-30 — only real "validation" in the diff is a referer/host string compare, narrow relative to the task's stated ambition (confidence=50, P3).
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the code’s only protection is a simple referer/host string comparison and implies this is weak validation. While it doesn’t explicitly mention the specific `indexOf`/substring bypass (e.g., `evil-discourseUrl.com`), it points to the same underlying issue: inadequate origin validation based on naive string matching.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15-29 — check-then-act TOCTOU on `embed.blank?`/`TopicEmbed.create!`; concurrent imports can raise unhandled RecordInvalid/RecordNotUnique, leaving an orphan Topic/Post outside the embed record (confidence=75, P2).

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does a non-atomic `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` check and then, if blank, proceeds to create a post and then `TopicEmbed.create!` for the same `embed_url`. The migration adds a **unique index** on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, so concurrent callers importing the same URL can both observe `embed.blank?` and race; the second will hit the unique constraint and raise (typically `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`, or potentially `RecordInvalid`). This exception is not rescued here, so it can fail the import/job. The proposed “orphan Topic/Post” part is less certain because the create happens inside a DB transaction (`Topic.transaction`), which would normally roll back the post/topic if the embed insert fails, but the unhandled race/exception itself is a real issue present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:44-52 — `open(url)` has no timeout/size limit, called synchronously inside a Sidekiq job; a hanging remote host blocks the worker, retry-enabled RetrieveTopic job compounds queue exhaustion (confidence=75, P2).

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), the code does `open(url).read` with no explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` or response size limit before passing the body to Readability. This method is invoked by `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, which is ultimately called from the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` Sidekiq job (`TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`). A slow/hanging or very large remote response can therefore block a Sidekiq worker thread for an unbounded/very long time and consume memory. Additionally, `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` does not set `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so it will use Sidekiq’s default retry behavior, potentially compounding queue exhaustion if the remote endpoint consistently hangs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:9-18 — staff users bypass throttle entirely (`no_throttle: true`); repeated requests can trigger many concurrent import_remote calls against the same host (confidence=50, P2).

adjudication.rationale: The job does pass `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` into `TopicRetriever`, and `retrieved_recently?` explicitly returns `false` when `@opts[:no_throttle]` is set. However, this is clearly intentional (comment: “We can disable the throttle for some users, such as staff”). The alleged “problem” (staff can trigger many concurrent `import_remote` calls) depends on staff repeatedly enqueueing jobs and on race timing before `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` flips to true; it’s not a clear defect introduced by the diff and is limited to trusted staff users. As written, the diff shows a deliberate bypass rather than an accidental vulnerability/bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:35-46 — non-atomic existence check before fetch gives false confidence duplicate work is prevented (confidence=50, P3).

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb `perform_retrieve` does `return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` and later proceeds to fetch/import. That check is not atomic with the subsequent creation path in `TopicEmbed.import` (`embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then `TopicEmbed.create!`). Under concurrency (e.g., multiple retrieve jobs, or scheduled feed polling + an embed fetch), two workers can both observe “no embed”, both do the expensive fetch, and one can hit the unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, raising on `create!` (no rescue shown). So the existence check can’t reliably prevent duplicate work and may lead to avoidable exceptions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — unconditional job enqueue per request with no requester-scoped rate limit; anonymous flood can enqueue unbounded RetrieveTopic jobs (confidence=50, P3).

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) returns nil, the code unconditionally does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` on every request. There is no de-duplication or rate limiting at enqueue time, and this path is reachable for anonymous users (current_user can be nil) as long as `ensure_embeddable` passes. Although TopicRetriever (invoked inside the job) has a Redis throttle, it happens during job execution, not before enqueueing, so a flood can still create an unbounded number of queued RetrieveTopic jobs (even for the same embed_url).

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:5-6 — `topic_id`/`post_id` columns have no index and no FK constraints; deleting a topic/post leaves dangling TopicEmbed rows (confidence=50, P3).

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb the table is created with topic_id and post_id columns but only an index on embed_url is added. There are no indexes on topic_id or post_id, and no foreign key constraints declared, so the database will not enforce referential integrity between topic_embeds and topics/posts. As a result, if a topic or post is deleted outside of any application-level cleanup, topic_embeds rows can become orphaned; and lookups by topic_id/post_id would require full scans.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:11 & app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33 — URL-scheme validation regex duplicated in two places, can drift out of sync (confidence=50, P3).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does contain two separate checks using the same URL-scheme regex (`/^https?\:\/\//`) in `TopicEmbed.import` and `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`. However, this is a maintainability/style concern (duplication) rather than a verifiable defect, correctness bug, or security issue introduced by the change. The claim that they “can drift out of sync” is speculative and not demonstrably problematic in the current diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `open(url).read` fetches attacker-influenced `embed_url` with only a hostname-equality check upstream; no scheme allowlist, no redirect/DNS-rebinding protection — potential SSRF to internal/metadata endpoints (confidence=50, P2).

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` on `url` ultimately derived from the request param `embed_url` (via `EmbedController#best` -> `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever` -> `fetch_http`). The only gate is `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, which compares `URI(@embed_url).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. That does not enforce an http/https scheme allowlist (e.g., `ftp://<allowed-host>/...`) and, more importantly, does not prevent SSRF via redirects: `open-uri` will follow HTTP redirects by default, so a URL on the allowed host can redirect to internal/metadata endpoints even though the initial hostname matched. DNS rebinding is also not mitigated. This is a concrete, diff-introduced SSRF risk path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:14-17 — `invalid_host?` checks hostname equality only, not scheme, not redirect chains — insufficient SSRF gate (confidence=50, P2).

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only compares `URI(@embed_url).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. The subsequent fetch (`TopicEmbed.import_remote`) does `open(url).read` via open-uri, which will follow HTTP redirects by default. So an attacker-controlled `embed_url` on the allowed host (or an open redirect on that host) can redirect the server to fetch arbitrary internal/external URLs, bypassing the host equality check. Additionally, `invalid_host?` does not restrict scheme, and `import_remote` has no `http/https` regex guard, so non-HTTP schemes (e.g., `ftp://allowed-host/...`) would also pass the host check and be fetched.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:56-76 + app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29-32 + app/models/post.rb:131-135 + app/views/embed/best.html.erb:20 — RSS-imported content flows unsanitized (only href/src rewritten) into a `raw_html` post rendered via `raw post.cooked` on both the embed view and standard topic view — stored XSS if feed source is compromised or less-trusted (confidence=75, P1).

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a new `cook_method` enum with a `:raw_html` option (app/models/post.rb) that makes `Post#cook` return `raw` directly, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, using `contents` sourced from RSS/Atom (`Jobs::PollFeed` parses `i.content` and passes it through only `CGI.unescapeHTML` plus URL absolutization of relative `href`/`src`). No HTML sanitization is applied to remove `<script>`, event handler attributes (`onerror`, `onclick`), `javascript:` URLs, etc. The embed view then renders this content with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), making stored XSS straightforward if the feed (or fetched remote content) is compromised or not fully trusted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:27-33 — Referer-header host check is fully client-controlled and trivially spoofed by non-browser clients; provides no real access control (confidence=75, P2).

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is gated by `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. The `Referer` header is supplied by the client and can be omitted or trivially spoofed by non-browser clients (e.g., curl setting an arbitrary Referer), so this check does not provide robust access control to `/embed/best` and the subsequent behavior (rendering embed content / enqueuing `:retrieve_topic`). This weakness is directly visible in lines 27–33 of the new controller.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:31 — `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` disables clickjacking protection for this controller, combined with the spoofable referer check, allows framing from arbitrary origins if embed_url is known/guessed (confidence=50, P3).
matched_golden_ids: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core security issue: setting `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` disables clickjacking protection and the protection relies on a spoofable Referer check, enabling arbitrary framing. It does not explicitly mention the nil-Referer fallback-to-empty-string masking validation failures, but it captures the main underlying vulnerability described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:14-19 — no explicit topic-visibility/permission check before building `TopicView`; relies entirely on unverifiable internal enforcement (confidence=25, suppressed per threshold but included as P2 due to potential impact) — retained as low-confidence note.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, the code does build `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` without an explicit permission check in this controller. However, the finding’s claim that this is a problem is not verifiable from the diff alone: `TopicView` is not modified here, and in typical Discourse architecture `TopicView`/Guardian enforces visibility/permissions internally. The diff introduces no evidence that permission checks are missing or bypassed, so the finding is speculative rather than a demonstrable defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:34,40 — stubs `retrieved_recently?` entirely, never exercises the real redis setnx/expire throttle logic (confidence=85, P2).

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb`, the two “valid host” examples explicitly stub `retrieved_recently?` to `true/false`, so they do not execute the real Redis-based throttle logic (`$redis.setnx`/`expire`). However, this is a test-design/coverage observation rather than a verifiable defect in the application code introduced by the diff; the tests are intentionally unit-testing `#retrieve`’s branching. The diff does not show an actual bug caused by this stubbing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb + spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb — full chain controller→retriever→import_remote→HTTP fetch/Readability parsing has no integration test anywhere (confidence=80, P2).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds unit/spec tests for `TopicRetriever` and `EmbedController`, and a model spec for `TopicEmbed.import`, but it does not include an end-to-end/integration spec that exercises the full path through `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (with `open(url)` + Readability parsing). However, the proposed finding is fundamentally about test coverage (absence of an integration test), not a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the code. Also, the claim “no integration test anywhere” cannot be proven from the diff alone because tests could exist elsewhere outside the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:44 — `import_remote` never called or asserted on in any spec (confidence=90, P2).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (app/models/topic_embed.rb:44) and no spec directly exercises or asserts behavior of `.import_remote` (the added `topic_embed_spec` only tests `.import`; other specs stub/mock `TopicRetriever` without executing `fetch_http`). However, this is a test-coverage observation rather than a verifiable bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the diff. The method is called by production code paths (`TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, `disqus.thor`), so “never called” is only true within specs and does not indicate a functional problem in the implementation itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:59 — `prefix << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443` — scheme-unaware port logic (e.g. http on 443) is completely untested; only default-port case exercised (confidence=65, P3).

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, `prefix` is built as `scheme://host` and then the port is appended only if `uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443`. This logic is scheme-unaware: it will *omit* port 443 even when the scheme is `http` (e.g., `http://example.com:443/...`) and omit port 80 when the scheme is `https` (e.g., `https://example.com:80/...`), producing incorrect absolute URLs. The added spec only exercises a URL without an explicit/non-default port, so this behavior is not covered by tests in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:131 — raw_html cook short-circuit only exercised indirectly via TopicEmbed integration spec, no direct/isolated Post unit test (confidence=50, P3).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `Post#cook` short-circuit for `cook_method == :raw_html`, and this behavior is indeed covered by `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` (it asserts `post.cooked == post.raw` when imported). The proposed finding is only that there is no *direct/isolated* unit test for `Post#cook` itself. That is a test-organization preference/testing gap, not a verifiable bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — `create_table :top_topics, force: true` added to an already-existing/previously-shipped migration file (confirmed unchanged in base commit); if replayed against any live DB with this migration already applied, silently DROPs and recreates top_topics, losing data with no backup/rollback step (confidence=90, P2).

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `CreateTopTopics` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists and recreate it. That introduces a real risk of silent data loss if this migration is ever re-run against a database that already has `top_topics` (e.g., via migrate:redo/reset, rebuilding an environment, or any situation where the migration executes while the table exists). Without `force: true` it would instead raise, preventing accidental destructive behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — `force: true` forward-path drop is an undocumented irreversible side effect not captured by Rails' change/rollback reversibility reporting (confidence=75, P2).

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an old migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. While `force: true` can drop an existing table before creating it, this migration only runs once in normal Rails usage. Existing installations that already ran this migration will not re-run it, and new installations won’t have `top_topics` yet, so there is no verifiable data-loss/correctness bug introduced by this change in the typical forward path. The finding is largely hypothetical and about migration style/edge cases (re-running migrations or pre-existing table), not a clear defect evidenced by the diff.
